case.prompt: What is a compiler? Answer in one concise sentence.
case.reference_text: A compiler translates source code into executable machine code.

case.prompt: Give a practical three-step checklist for investigating a program that suddenly uses too much memory.
case.reference_text: Measure memory over time, identify the largest allocations, and inspect retained references or caches. Reproduce the growth with a small workload before changing code.

case.prompt: Compare breadth-first search and depth-first search for traversing a graph. Explain how their frontier differs, name one problem for which each is a natural choice, and mention the memory trade-off on a wide graph. Then outline how a visited set prevents repeated work, what changes when edges have weights, and why the usual shortest-path guarantee depends on those weights. Include a small discussion of disconnected graphs, cycles, and how a priority queue changes the traversal when nonnegative edge costs matter. Relate the discussion to adjacency lists versus matrices, recursive stack limits, deterministic neighbor ordering, and reconstruction of a path from predecessor links; make clear which claims apply only to unweighted graphs and which require nonnegative costs.
case.reference_text: Breadth-first search uses a queue and explores by distance, making it natural for shortest unweighted paths. Depth-first search uses a stack or recursion and suits reachability or backtracking; on a wide graph, breadth-first search can use more memory.
